_notes: What a pastor of the diocese writes to the prior for. E3 §3.12. The pastor asks the prior, never the friar; the prior says yes when the house can spare the blocks, and only then does the friar see it, for six weeks. Effects land when the work is done. Tunables invented.

asks.label: A parish mission
asks.blurb: Four evenings in Lent, the old kind, in a parish that has not had one since the seventies.
asks.costs: four weeks of evenings and the drive, and the horarium covered while you are gone

asks.label: Sunday supply while he is away
asks.blurb: His Masses for a month: he has not had a holiday in four years and the bishop's office has no one.
asks.costs: four Sundays and the Saturday evening, for a month

asks.label: Confessions on Saturdays
asks.blurb: His Saturday afternoons, since his people have stopped coming to him and would come to a friar.
asks.costs: an afternoon a week for half a year

asks.label: His parish's retreat weekend
asks.blurb: A Friday night and a Saturday for his parish council and the people who run things, at the retreat house.
asks.costs: a weekend, and the talks written

asks.label: Forty Hours and the closing homily
asks.blurb: His parish's Forty Hours: the exposition, the holy hours, and the friar to preach the closing.
asks.costs: three days in his church and a homily the parish will repeat

asks.label: The school's Mass and confessions
asks.blurb: His parish school's Friday Mass and the children's confessions before Christmas and Easter, since he cannot get through them alone.
asks.costs: a Friday morning a week for a season

asks.label: A talk at the deanery's clergy day
asks.blurb: An afternoon for the priests of the deanery on the thing you know, since the dean has heard you know it.
